topic.subject: science
topic.title: Chemical effects of electric current
topic.scope: conduction in liquids, electrolysis basics, electroplating, tester with LED

nodes.name: Tap water and salt solutions conduct
Metal transfer from anode to cathode

misconceptions.statement: Pure distilled water conducts electricity just like tap water.
misconceptions.why: Students generalize their experience that water and electricity are a dangerous combination.
misconceptions.fix: Distilled water is free of salts and is a poor conductor; it does not conduct electricity.

probe.question: If you use a battery and a bulb with pure distilled water, will the bulb glow?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because water is a conductor.

misconceptions.root_belief: All forms of a substance behave identically.

misconceptions.statement: If the bulb in a tester does not glow, no current is flowing through the liquid.
misconceptions.why: Students rely on visible light as the only indicator of electrical flow.
misconceptions.fix: The current might be too weak to make the bulb glow; an LED or magnetic compass is needed for weak currents.

probe.question: A student tests lemon juice with a bulb tester and it doesn't glow. Is there current?
probe.wrong_answer: No, the circuit is broken because the bulb is off.

misconceptions.root_belief: No visible effect means no underlying process.

misconceptions.statement: It doesn't matter which way you connect the two wires of an LED.
misconceptions.why: Standard bulbs work regardless of orientation, so students apply this to LEDs.
misconceptions.fix: An LED has polarity; the longer lead must be connected to the positive terminal.

probe.question: Why did the LED not glow even though the circuit was complete?
probe.wrong_answer: The LED is probably fused or the battery is dead.

misconceptions.root_belief: Symmetry in components implies identical function.

misconceptions.statement: The bubbles formed during electrolysis are just the water boiling.
misconceptions.why: Bubbles in water are most commonly associated with boiling in everyday life.
misconceptions.fix: The bubbles are actually gases like oxygen and hydrogen produced by a chemical reaction.

probe.question: What are the bubbles seen near the electrodes in water electrolysis?
probe.wrong_answer: Steam or water vapor from heating.

misconceptions.source_hint: Rosalind Driver's Children's Ideas in Science

misconceptions.statement: In electroplating, the metal atoms travel through the air or jump directly between plates.
misconceptions.why: Students struggle to visualize the role of the solution in transporting ions.
misconceptions.fix: Metal ions from the solution deposit on the cathode, and the anode dissolves to replenish the solution.

probe.question: How does copper get from one plate to the other in a copper sulfate solution?
probe.wrong_answer: It moves through the water without changing into anything else.

misconceptions.root_belief: Matter moves directly from source to destination.

misconceptions.statement: Liquids conduct electricity using free electrons just like copper wires.
misconceptions.why: Students carry over the model of metallic conduction to all states of matter.
misconceptions.fix: Liquids conduct electricity through the movement of ions, not free electrons.

probe.question: What carries the electric charge through a salt solution?

misconceptions.root_belief: Mechanism in one state applies to all states.

misconceptions.statement: Iron is coated with zinc because zinc is 'stronger' than iron.
misconceptions.why: Students use everyday meanings of 'strong' to explain protection.
misconceptions.fix: Zinc is used because it is more reactive and prevents the iron underneath from rusting.

probe.question: Why do we plate iron bridge girders with zinc?
probe.wrong_answer: To make the iron harder and harder to break.

misconceptions.root_belief: A word means its everyday meaning.

misconceptions.statement: Adding sugar to water makes it a good conductor because the sugar dissolves.
misconceptions.fix: Sugar dissolves as molecules, not ions, so sugar solution does not conduct electricity.

probe.question: Will a circuit be completed if you use a sugar solution?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because the sugar has dissolved in the water.

misconceptions.root_belief: Dissolving always produces mobile charged particles.

misconceptions.statement: Electricity 'creates' the metal that is deposited on the electrode.
misconceptions.why: The appearance of new solid metal seems like creation from energy.
misconceptions.fix: Electricity only provides the energy to move existing metal ions from the solution to the electrode.

probe.question: Where does the copper on the spoon come from during electroplating?
probe.wrong_answer: The electricity turns into copper when it hits the spoon.

misconceptions.root_belief: Energy can be directly converted into matter.

misconceptions.statement: The magnetic needle moves because the liquid itself becomes a magnet.
misconceptions.why: Students misattribute the magnetic field of the wire to the liquid in the beaker.
misconceptions.fix: The needle moves because the current in the wire wrapped around the compass creates a magnetic field.

probe.question: Why does the compass needle deflect when the tester leads are dipped in lemon juice?
probe.wrong_answer: Because lemon juice is magnetic when electricity is in it.

misconceptions.root_belief: The nearest object is the cause of the effect.

misconceptions.statement: Chromium plating is done to make the whole object out of chromium.
misconceptions.why: Students don't distinguish between a surface coating and the bulk material.
misconceptions.fix: Only a thin layer of chromium is deposited to save costs while providing shine and rust resistance.

probe.question: Is a 'chrome' bicycle handle made entirely of chromium?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, that is why it is so shiny and doesn't rust.

misconceptions.root_belief: The surface represents the whole object.

misconceptions.statement: The liquid in the beaker is just there to hold the electrodes and doesn't participate.
misconceptions.why: The liquid looks unchanged to the naked eye during the early stages.
misconceptions.fix: The electrolyte is essential as it provides the ions that carry the current and provide the metal for plating.

probe.question: Can we use plain distilled water for copper plating if the copper plates are present?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, the water just needs to let the electricity pass between plates.

misconceptions.root_belief: If a substance doesn't disappear, it isn't reacting.
